x: The handicap was won by "new boy" Ken Baily; to see the best of him we will have to wait until the distance season---16yr old Gerry Cameron took second place.

Vic Townsend and Gerry Cameron showed what pack training can do, and Don Bartliff walked well for his first "Open" in Belgrave colours. What? no Belgrave man or team in the handicap?---shame! perhaps they are saving it!
Unfortunately we are painfully short of Juniors for this event and open competition generally, but nevertheless, Gerry Cameron walked well to win this trophy for the 2nd year running.

It was encouraging to see Gerry Cameron finish so well in this his first try-out over 10 miles and also to have Bernard Eglinton back home again after three years abroad and pushing the lads once more.
Gerry Cameron produced a surprise packet when in only his second 10 mile race he came through to finish our third man home, 32nd in 88:27 with Cyril Yescombe not far away in 38th position.
Also in close attendance were Will Belderson and Ken Bailey with Gerry Cameron again giving us a pleasant surprise by finishing first of the 'B' team in 23rd place.
Morris (28th in 61:11) were our other finishers. In the supporting road events, Gerry Cameron walked very well in the Junior 6 miles, to finish 5th in 51 minutes.

Consequently we were nowhere in the team Championship, although Bob Barnes walked most creditably, considering the absence of support, to finish 12th in 57:24. Gerry Cameron (24th in 60:06) carried off the third individual handicap and Joe Wilson took first Veterans' prize.

Our only representatives in the National Youths and Junior Walks at Battersea Park on October 20th were Gerry Cameron and Brian Bushman who finished 18th and 36th respectively in the Junior Event. 55 Started.
There were only two competitors in the 5 miles Club Championship for Juniors. Dave King was the winner in 42:05, with Gerry Cameron clocking 43:43.
Ray Middleton finished second in the '2' with Ted Smith 9th. Non-scorers from all clubs were allowed to take part in this race and first of those to finish was Gerry Cameron in 14th position.
Four 'Bels' Ray Middleton, John Knifton, Bob Barnes and Gerald Cameron were in the party and the first two names ensured that the claret and gold was carried very prominently.

Jack Goswell is enthusiastic about their potential and considers that with Gerry Cameron (still only 20) we have a quartet worth watching. We hear that STAN VICKERS has just left the Hospital for Tropical Diseases after being detained for observation.
BOTTOM RIGHT:John Morris receives refreshment from Fred Denny, with John Keown alongside. Gerry Cameron follows by bicyle.
In the individual handicap Dave King was 2nd and Gerry Cameron 7th, and these two with the help of Steve Laker-Jones and John Knifton won the handicap team race
To these add the fast improving LAKER-JONES, GERRY CAMERON, and the future looks safe indeed. It is an interesting fact that we started 4 International walkers in our teams.
At the Middlesex track '7' at Parliament Hill on April, 8th Steve Laker/Jones was unplaced with a time of 58:50 and Gerry Cameron was "pulled".

Gerry Cameron has sent us several articles on training which were first published in Belgrave newsletters in the early 1950's. These will be appearing from time to time - the first one being by Harry Churcher.
Gerry Cameron won the "Horwood Cup" for the 1965 Club Junior '7'. His time of 61:53 was 49 seconds better than runner-up Bob Picton, but Bob got his revenge in the handicap by taking first prize.

In the Southern R.W.A "Garnet Cup" 10 miles at Bexley on February 6th, Gerry Cameron walked very strongly to finish 12th in 85:59. Our winning team of last year was barred from this event so we did quite well to finish 5th.

We have Eric Hall in Leicester, Gerry Cameron in Market Harborough, Bob Barnes in Cambridge, Bob Farley in Loughborough, Dave King in Bournemouth, John Knifton in U.S.A. and Bill Newhill back in Coventry.
Gerry Cameron showed surprising form in the 'B' race, finishing 2nd behind Hughes of Smethwick. Bob Barnes also walked well to finish 4th, just 143 yds behind his team-mate.

Held on the day of our opening '5', Steve Laker-Jones and Ray Hall travelled to join our three 'local' lads, Eric Hall, Gerry Cameron, and Bob Farley (having his first outing since returning from Germany and joining Loughborough College).

The team,consisting of "Yo Yo" Hall (he goes downhill alright but can't climb 'em) Ray Hall,the chaffeur; Gerry Cameron, the 2nd fastest Scot; and Steve Laker Jones, at present tail end Charlie, were helped out this time by Harry Shields.
Gerry Cameron won the Senior '6' at the "Hinckley Times" Meeting on September 11th.

Gerry Cameron was unable to get down from the Midlands and Hamlin, Mayo and Farley were unexpectedly away, with the result that only 10 of our 23 entries finished, and we were unplaced in the team event.

Eric Hall shaped well and Gerry Cameron continued to ride on a crest of a wave with another excellent performance. Herding them in close behind was Ray Hall who, although not yet full fit, walked a real captain's race---his 19th position ensuring us of a second team place.
Gerry Cameron is riding high these days and is sufficiently self-confident to take the Editors to task for suggesting that Eric Hall had helped him along at Leicester.
Gerry Cameron was in brilliant form over our own 7 mile course the week before Christmas. His four minutes margin over Ray Hall enabled him to win both the match and the Junior Championship.

Gerry Cameron came down from Leicester to boost our team in the first 'open' of 1966 and enabled us to gain an encouraging second place. Several of the 188 starters came under the judges' ban and Met WC lost McCullagh and Watts, a set-back from which they did well to recover.

Gerry Cameron made a gallant attempt to get away from his main rivals, Middleton and Hall, by going away with Police walker David Watts. At 5 miles he was still ahead going through in 39:13 to Ray Hall's 39:19 and Middleton's 39:34 but the distance experts came into their own in the second half and…
Gerry Cameron did well once again to get amongst the medals but an eight minutes wait for our next man ruled out any hopes of a similar team success.

The Belgrave 1966 20 miles Club Champion is Ray Middleton (2:41:43) who won from Ray Hall (2:55:29) and Gerry Cameron (2:56:43). Ray Hall was a good winner of the Stock Exchange 25 miles championship at Hayes on April 2nd, winning by over 8 minutes (3:41:21) from his old rival Dicky Green (SWC).

With any luck he will then settle down as a P.E.teacher somewhere in Surrey and with some further luck produce some even better form, Gerry Cameron is one up on Bob, having just become a father for the second time - think of it, three Camerons!
His 8th position, only 2:04 down on Middleton must have been one of his best ever performances. Gerry Cameron (not at his best) and the fast improving Jack Baker completed our scoring four.
Bob Barnes is walking very well these days and could surprise in the National '10' With Gerry Cameron also walking into form the teams could well click at the right time.
Duquemin of the Channel Island club, Sarnia. His time of 77:55 was 5:43 faster than our own Gerry Cameron who finished 7th.
Pat Duncan paid for an over enthusiastic start over the second ten miles but with Ray Hall, Gerry Cameron and Bob Farley dropping out, finished an unworried second.
Gerry Cameron quashed the rumour that he had finally retired to stud by finishing second in 57m 35secs.
In the Welsh 20 Kilos Gerry Cameron finished 11th in 113m 26 secs. Bernie Capener finished 14th in 116m 55 secs and won the handicap.

43 Walkers took this opportunity to work off their Christmas excesses with Paul Nihill leading them home in 52.42. Gerry Cameron improved on his recent form to take the Handicap with an actual time of 57.43
Bob Farley suprised himself and the Handicapper by beating Gerry Cameron by over a minute.

Gerry Cameron and Dave Mayo are both going great guns at the moment and Bob Farley lacks none of his old fire. Ray Hall too seemed to have taken on a new lease of life although his recent exploits with the paint brush have set him back a bit.
Gerry Cameron and Ray Middleton during the Club '20'
The Championship was ours from the start, with Len Duquemin, Bob Barnes and John Moullin completing the team, closely supported by Gerry Cameron.

Gerry Cameron had some rude things to say when lapped by one of his clubmates but soon recovered to finish his first 50 Kilos in fine form. Bernard Eglinton also turned in a useful performance so that had the captain been a prophet we could also have taken the Milan Trophy for the first team to finish eight.

In the Leicester Open '7' Gerry Cameron led the Belgrave contingent home in a classy 55.32. Gerry is in the process of moving to Swindon but we will be needing performances like this in 1969 to keep our place at the top.

True Bobby Barnes is not yet back to the form (or shape!) of a year ago and it is some time since we have seen or heard Dave Mayo but Carl Lawton and Brian Ward are both showing steady improvement and Gerry Cameron is also going well.
Brian Ward, Gerry Cameron and Bob Picton all looked to be on the trail again and up north Dave King and Paul Duckett are sure to be slipping in some crafty sessions.

Both Gerry Cameron and Bob Coates have as their ambition representing the host country Scotland. Gerry, who did much work behind the scenes to get race walking re-established in Scotland a couple of years ago, will find it very difficult to make the team.

Gerry Cameron is back training although his recent move to Scotland is something of a problem. Another much improved walker is Bernard Capener who should feature in the international postman's walk in September.
Gerry Cameron has been putting walking on to the Scottish map although support from South of the border is lacking due to distance. Maybe the Bels can get a team up there next year.

Gerry Cameron, after a long trip down from Dunfermline, held off Ray Hall. Finally came Pat Duncan, and although many of the walkers at the front went off faster than him he was unable to pull them back again when he began to "come through" with 20 yards to go.

Little mention has been made of the work being done by our 'North of the Border' paid up member Gerry Cameron. Our roving correspondent, however, whilst on a round trip, discovered Gerry hiding in the small village of Carnock, in the shadow of Dunfermline.
1968 · Winners (Ray Middleton, Len Duquemin, Bob Barnes, Gerry Cameron)

These performances would not have been possible without help on the road by others so a tribute to the selfless efforts of Charlie McLennan, Jack Goswell, Bob Barnes, Gerry Cameron, Bob Picton, Carl Lawton and Pat Duncan, and when not competing against him, John Morris.
